topic.title: Who your RM works for
topic.claim: The relationship manager who calls you 'sir' and remembers your birthday earns more when you buy the product that's worse for you.
topic.moment: The bank RM visits with a 'guaranteed return' plan that is half insurance, half investment.

turn.believed: The RM is the bank's free advisor for me.
turn.actually: The RM is a salesperson with targets, and some products pay far better commissions than others.

topic.feeling: Naive for trusting the friendliest person at the bank.
topic.villain: Cross-sell targets and commission structures inside banks
topic.because: Insurance-linked plans pay higher commissions than a plain FD or index fund. The warmth is real, and so is the target.
topic.payoff: Ask your RM one question: 'What do you earn if I buy this?' Watch how long the answer takes.
topic.behaviour: RMs push ULIPs and endowment plans to salaried customers and to their parents.
topic.mechanism: The product that pays the seller most gets pitched hardest.
topic.group: Salaried account holders and their parents
topic.send_to: Their parents, who just got a call from the bank
topic.why_now: Bonus and year-end tax-saving season is when the RM calls start.
topic.needs_facts: That commissions on insurance-linked products are higher than on plain deposits, from IRDAI or SEBI disclosures

score.why: The friendly bank RM is a salesperson with a target, and the question 'what do you earn?' is a test readers can run. A natural one to send to parents.

sources.fact: IRDAI's September 2026 draft distribution reforms would bar volume-linked and reward-linked incentives for bank and NBFC staff selling insurance, and list ULIPs sold to risk-averse or post-working-age customers as mis-selling that can trigger commission claw-back.
sources.excerpt: "ULIPs to risk-averse or post-working-age customers" is one of twelve codified illustrations. Mis-selling can trigger commission claw-back. | "Volume-linked and reward-linked incentives for bank and NBFC staff selling insurance are prohibited." | Individual life (premium term of 10+ years): IDEs face a 20% first-year cap and 3% on renewal. (These are proposed rules, not final.)

sources.fact: A 1 Finance insurance adviser says commissions are built into premiums and that policies combining savings or investment with insurance pay distributors higher upfront payouts than term plans, which have thinner margins.
sources.excerpt: "A significant part of the answer lies in how insurance distribution is structured in India." "Commissions are embedded within premiums and vary considerably across product types." "Policies that combine insurance with savings or investment elements typically offer higher upfront payouts to distributors." "Pure protection products, like term plans, operate on considerably thinner margins."

sources.fact: All India Radio reports that IRDAI proposed prohibiting volume-linked or reward-linked incentives for bank and NBFC staff selling insurance, and tighter measures against mis-selling and compulsory bundling.
sources.excerpt: "prohibiting volume-linked or reward-linked incentives for bank and Non-Banking Financial Company staff selling insurance" | "tighter measures to curb mis-selling and compulsory bundling of insurance with other financial products" | "bringing direct and indirect remuneration within the regulatory definition of commission"

draft.caption: What's the 'guaranteed return' plan your RM pitched to you or your parents, and did anyone ever ask what it paid the bank?
draft.alt_text: A nine-slide text post about bank relationship managers in India. It argues that the friendly RM is a salesperson with a target, not a free advisor. It notes that IRDAI's proposed draft rules would ban volume-linked and reward-linked incentives for bank staff selling insurance, that insurance-plus-investment plans pay the bank more upfront than term plans, FDs or index funds, and that the same draft lists a ULIP sold to someone past working age as mis-selling, the very plan parents get called about. It shows parents signing at the branch because the bank said it was safe, while the target counts what got sold, not whether it fit. It ends with one question for the RM, 'What do you earn if I buy this?', an answer that comes slower than the birthday wish.

claims.text: IRDAI's draft distribution rules would prohibit volume-linked and reward-linked incentives for bank and NBFC staff selling insurance; these are proposed rules, not final.
Commissions are built into insurance premiums, and plans that mix insurance with savings pay distributors such as banks higher upfront payouts than term plans, which have thinner margins.
Insurance-linked plans pay higher commissions than a plain FD or index fund.
The RM is a salesperson with targets.
IRDAI's draft rules list ULIPs sold to post-working-age customers as mis-selling.
